subject.title: [Feature]: Option to force-prepend an opening <think> tag for local reasoning models

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class default-off synthetic `<think>` opener option, or should model-specific thinking/delimiter handling remain provider-owned through params and catalog metadata?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a new output-format/config contract is compatibility-sensitive and VISION.md favors keeping core lean unless existing provider/plugin seams are insufficient.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core option
options.body: Add one documented default-off config path, wire it through runner/subscriber params, and prove streaming plus final-message behavior with native-tag and no-tag cases.

options.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
options.body: Use existing provider params/catalog metadata for model-specific thinking behavior and only add a core delimiter option if maintainers confirm those seams cannot cover the observed models.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject frontend-side delimiter synthesis and ask reporters to use provider/model prompt or request settings instead.

recommendation.title: Prefer provider-owned controls first
recommendation.body: Use existing provider params/catalog metadata for model-specific thinking behavior and only add a core delimiter option if maintainers confirm those seams cannot cover the observed models.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant config, embedded-agent, and reasoning-tag paths are mostly in recent Peter Steinberger commits and prior maintainer review comments route the decision there.
